name: Use calibrated computational evidence for missense variants (PP3/BP4)
description: Which predictor and score thresholds give calibrated ACMG/AMP computational evidence (PP3/BP4) for a missense variant in a gene without a gene-specific calibration, and at what strength?

attributes.question: Which predictor and score thresholds give calibrated ACMG/AMP computational evidence (PP3/BP4) for a missense variant in a gene without a gene-specific calibration, and at what strength?
intended_users: Clinical scientists classifying germline variants under ACMG/AMP criteria
Variant curation expert panels deciding whether to adopt or replace genome-wide thresholds
attributes.decision: Choose one predictor in advance and the score thresholds at which it supplies PP3 or BP4 evidence at Supporting, Moderate or Strong strength, for a missense variant in a gene with no gene-specific calibration.
inputs: A germline missense variant on a stated transcript and genome build
The chosen predictor's precomputed score at a pinned version
Whether a gene- or region-specific specification exists that supersedes genome-wide thresholds
attributes.output: Calibrated score intervals for each evidence strength per predictor, the highest strength each reaches, the calibration data and its limits, and independent rankings of the same predictors. No variant classification.
attributes.setting: Germline missense variants assessed under ACMG/AMP criteria. The genome-wide calibrations use ClinVar pathogenic and benign missense variants rare in gnomAD, from genes with at least one pathogenic variant, with tools' training variants removed where available, and a prior probability of pathogenicity of 4.41% estimated from gnomAD.
exclusions: Genes with an expert-panel specification that sets its own thresholds (BRCA1/BRCA2 is a separate use case)
Splicing, in-frame indel, protein-truncating and non-coding variants
Combining several predictors, or counting PP3 together with overlapping evidence such as PM1 or allele frequency beyond the recommended caps
Final variant classification or patient management
attributes.clinical_scope: Clinical research on the evidence strength of computational predictions. Calibrated thresholds hold on average across genes; they do not classify a variant and do not replace expert review.
evidence_gaps: The four tools that reach PP3_Strong in Pejaver et al. 2022 (BayesDel, MutPred2, REVEL, VEST4) each have a developer among that paper's authors; no independent recalibration of them is in the store.
The calibrations are genome-wide; Tejura et al. 2024 show that gene-level performance of REVEL and BayesDel often departs from them. No gene-level calibration is extracted.

Thirteen predictors have four-level intervals (Pejaver et al. 2022) and seven have points-scale intervals (Bergquist et al. 2025). Newer predictors ranked highly by Livesey and Marsh 2025 (for example popEVE, CPT-1) have no ClinGen calibration in the store.
Pejaver et al. 2022 Table S1 (point estimates and one-sided confidence bounds) was not retrieved.

A 2026 Genetics in Medicine calibration of machine-learning predictors (doi:10.1016/j.gim.2026.102606) is closed access and was not retrieved; the BayesQuantify (J Med Genet 2025) and P-KNN (bioRxiv 2025) joint calibrations were found but not extracted.
Evidence yield in real genomes (Stenton et al. 2024 Table 2) and reclassification impact (Dubé et al. 2026, Genet Med Open) were found but not extracted.
The Livesey and Marsh and ProteinGym rankings measure discrimination, not calibrated evidence strength; they help choose which predictors to calibrate, not which thresholds to apply.
Qualified human scientific review is outstanding; automated transcription does not establish replication.

name: PP3/BP4 score intervals on the points scale (Bergquist et al. 2025 Table 1)
description: Score interval of seven missense predictors for each point value from −4 to +4 of the ACMG/AMP points-based system, including the 3-point level and the indeterminate range.

attributes.protocol: Same data and calibration as Pejaver et al. 2022; report the score interval for Strong (±4), the 3-point level, Moderate (±2), Supporting (±1) and Indeterminate (0). Very Strong was never reached and is not shown.
attributes.metric_implementation: Local posterior probability of pathogenicity estimated in a sliding score window on the ClinVar 2019 set with prior 0.0441; a threshold is the most lenient score at which the one-sided 95% bootstrap bound (10,000 iterations) of the local positive likelihood ratio still reaches the cut-off for that strength (2.406, 5.790, 33.53, 1,124; reciprocals for BP4)
attributes.version: Bergquist et al. 2025, Table 1
attributes.source_locator: Table 1 and caption; Materials and Methods
limitations: Calibration is genome-wide (average over genes); Tejura et al. 2024 report that about 70% of the gene-level REVEL and BayesDel intervals with enough control variants exceeded the number of incorrect predictions the genome-wide recommendations imply.
Labels are ClinVar classifications; the authors assume computational evidence had no major role in them (Stenton et al. 2024, Table 1).

AlphaMissense, ESM1b and VARITY_R are calibrated in this paper; the BayesDel, MutPred2, REVEL and VEST4 rows keep the thresholds of Pejaver et al. 2022 and add the 3-point and indeterminate intervals (caption).

No training-set filtering was done for the new tools: only VARITY was trained on ClinVar, and its precomputed score for each variant comes from a model that excluded that variant (Materials and Methods).
The developer thresholds of AlphaMissense (0.564) and ESM1b (−7.5) do not reach Supporting for PP3 or BP4 under this calibration (Results).
V. Pejaver and P. Radivojac (MutPred2; Pejaver also REVEL) are authors. The BayesDel, MutPred2, REVEL and VEST4 rows come from Pejaver et al. 2022, whose authors include the developers of all four.
Some of the previously calibrated tools did not reach the likelihood ratios expected for the 3-point intervals when the authors checked them (Results, Fig. 1B).
The caption says Very Strong was never reached, but Pejaver et al. 2022 Table 2 gives a BP4 Very Strong interval for REVEL (≤0.003); here REVEL's Strong (−4) interval, ≤ 0.016, covers both.

The authors state that this calibration shares the limitations of the previous study: representativeness of the data, potential circularities, prior probability estimation and gene- or disease-specific variability (Discussion).
